steps.content: This is the first time you've met Lysandra after that nerve-wracking but ultimately harmless escape room adventure.
Though it's been only two days, and Nightingale has already swiftly delivered the additional materials you requested, somehow you still feel that time has been passing exceptionally slowly.
Lysandra, meanwhile, has lost the composed demeanor she displayed when first detained by the Bureau, looking restless and distracted.
The clearest sign being that since entering the interrogation room, she's been constantly shifting the thin stick in her mouth, and the coin she usually fidgets with is notably missing from her hand.
You organize the documents in your hands, preparing to begin the interrogation.
test
test
test
test
test
test

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Since N.F. 114, there have been a series of artifact thefts along the border between WhiteSands and DisCity. Our investigation has determined that all the trafficking routes can be traced back to a single source.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This individual has committed multiple offenses in unregulated zones throughout WhiteSands, including unauthorized entry into archaeological sites, artifact smuggling, and illegal reselling.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: That person is you, isn't it, Lysandra?

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: Correct. Thought I could feed the living with what the dead no longer needed.
She glances away as she answers casually.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: I have the skills to extract those things the dead have no use for, turning them into food and shelter for the living. They gain new value rather than just rotting beside corpses as worthless junk.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: The dead never complain, so I don't see why not.
You produce one of the photos from your new file. It's an ancient tomb the MBCC has tracked down which contains Lysandra's traces. The interior has been completely ransacked.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: During your excavations, you only ever took the most valuable treasures.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You were turning sites filled with invaluable historical records and precious artifacts into ruins, making it impossible for scholars to study the evolution of civilizations.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Furthermore, evidence of your method can be clearly seen at the edges of the tomb. You've caused extensive destruction.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: First, timing and opportunity are key in tomb raiding. Any excess weight that restricts movement can mean death for a tomb raider. That's why I only select the most valuable treasures to bring with me.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: I've seen plenty of greedy tomb raiders who tried to take everything. It only cost every single one of them their lives.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: Second, I destroy my traces for my own safety. Once I discover a tomb location, others will swarm in like flies, all wanting their share of the spoils.
Lysandra sits up straight.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: I must say, your people have got keen eyes to have identified me despite that level of destruction.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It's thanks to our Mania detector. We picked up traces of your Mania in that area.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: Mania detector...

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: Heh, I see, some fancy gadget those of us in WhiteSands would never know about.
You don't miss the momentary flicker in Lysandra's eyes.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: That covers the basic information. Now, let's discuss other matters.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: First of all, thank you. I know if that game had been real, I would've already died in that quicksand without you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'm surrounded by so many extraordinary people, including those like Roulecca who are naturally blessed with exceptional luck. Getting help from them feels like good fortune simply falling into my lap.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But I know there are hidden struggles and painful pasts behind all this, things they'd rather not mention. The luck I experience is only the surface of the story.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: So... I'd like to understand you better, to learn about the struggles that shaped you. If you're willing to share.
You close the dossier and quietly observe Lysandra, who has been cooperative throughout. She returns your gaze, the corner of her mouth curling slightly in a composed smile.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: I'm not much of a talker, but ask and I'll answer.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: OK.
Your eyes meet hers as you begin carefully.
You take out the coin engraved with the number eight and place it in front of Lysandra.
Her eyes dart away as you slowly push the coin toward her. When her breathing noticeably shallows, you stop considerately.
She pauses, then speaks calmly after a few seconds, as if the brief agitation has just been your imagination.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: The coin belonged to the geezers. A keepsake of some sort they left behind.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: After they died, I took one. That's all.
She answers your question, but only in the most technical sense.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: A gang of tomb raiders from WhiteSands who scraped by looting ancient ruins. Same job I do now.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: When they traveled around, they'd take in orphans they came across. I was one of them.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: I survived on the jobs they gave me, and it was always feast or famine.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: Eventually they went into a tomb and never came out. After that, I was on my own.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: What about the other children who were with you?

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: I don't know.
She gives a quick answer and shuts her mouth. Until now, she's only been telling you what you already know.
Her response now is markedly different from how she handled your questions about the artifact thefts earlier. She knows what you want to know. She just doesn't want to say it.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Let's cut to the chase, Lysandra.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The file I initially received about you contained only a few pages. Based on these pieces, the average person would piece together your story like this:

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: A poor orphan was taken in by a group of WhiteSands tomb raiders and grew up happily alongside other children. But to survive, the aging raiders had to take up a risky job and ended up all perishing in a cave-in. Only you, the lucky one, survived.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: They were the only family you had, the mentors who taught you how to survive, and an eternal memory...
You point at the coin worn to a shine.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But that's not how the story really goes, is it?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: No, I mean, maybe it did start that way...
You produce another document. You can feel Lysandra's body tense.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: How much do you know?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You're clever and careful enough. Just as you erase your tracks in tombs, you've also removed quite a bit of evidence of your story.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But when the MBCC wants to know something, nothing escapes us.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: What are you trying to s...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: They didn't die in a cave-in, did they?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: At the entrance of the ancient tomb where they disappeared, we found evidence of your sabotage, Lysandra.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It carried your Mania, the highest M-Value we've ever recorded from you in all our investigations and tests.
You pause for a few seconds.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: They didn't die in a cave-in...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You killed them, Lysandra.
After a silent moment similar to the one you shared in the escape room, you hear a soft laugh.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: ...Of course they didn't die in a cave-in.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: It was just...

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: Bad luck.
Her eyes trace the coin in front of her before she looks up at you with a mocking smile.
(Flashback)

steps.speaker: Scrawny Boy
steps.content: ...Lysandra, hey, they're getting impatient about the drawing. Everyone's waiting for you!

steps.speaker: Scrawny Boy
steps.content: Wake up! Old Fernando found a water source. Whoever volunteers to go down into the tomb gets a jar of water... Cough, cough, I'm so thirsty... but...

steps.speaker: Scrawny Boy
steps.content: But I don't want to end up unlucky like Noah and Jacob, who went in and never came back.
The scrawny boy stands with a limp, his hands clasped against his chest as he wipes snot and tears from his face with his arm.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: Miguel, your leg...

steps.speaker: Miguel
steps.content: I didn't clean up their dishes yesterday fast enough... so they beat me.

steps.speaker: Miguel
steps.content: If Noah and Jacob couldn't make it back even with their healthy bodies, I'm totally doomed...

The sandy wind picks up, burying Miguel's sobs. Hot grains sting their faces, blurring their vision as Lysandra weakly rises to her feet. From the distant edge of the rock, where rare patches of shade offer respite, comes the cursing of the old bastards.

steps.speaker: Rough Shouting Voice
steps.content: Get over here, you useless things! Come now or I'll send both of you down to scout that tomb today!

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: Don't be afraid. Let's go.
[Beside the rock]

steps.speaker: Tanned Boy
steps.content: Everyone listen to me! Three, two, one...
Miguel's hands tremble as he turns over the coin. Number eight. He's doomed.
A hand swiftly grabs the number eight coin from him, swapping it with another. Miguel nearly cries out in shock.

steps.speaker: Tanned Boy
steps.content: Who has the number eight coin... Number eight... Phew, it's Lysandra.
Lysandra stands expressionless, opening her palm to reveal the coin engraved with the number eight.

steps.speaker: Miguel
steps.content: It's Lysandra. She drew the number eight coin... How nice. We're all too unlucky...
As Miguel stammers through his words, Old Fernando cracks the whip in his hand. The sound of it ripping the air makes every child present tremble with fear.

steps.speaker: Old Fernando
steps.content: Hurry up! Who drew the number eight coin? Step forward now.

steps.speaker: Old Fernando
steps.content: Ah, it's you, Lysandra.

He swirls the battered flask in his hand. Lysandra's lips are cracked from dryness, her clothes are in tatters, and her face is covered in sand. Hearing the sound of water sloshing inside the flask, she involuntarily swallows, her throat burning like fire.
Old Fernando bares his teeth, satisfied with her reaction. He tosses a dagger and an old rope at her, then points behind himself.

steps.speaker: Old Fernando
steps.content: Let's see if today's your lucky day.
[Flashback to the interrogation room]
Lysandra reaches out and picks up the coin, examining it as if seeing it for the first time.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: Let me think, where to begin... Let's start with those old bastards who took in the orphans so benevolently.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: They scoured WhiteSands for homeless orphans, taking in anyone who was still breathing. Then they turned us into their expendable scouts.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: They made them draw coins to decide which child would enter the tombs as their scout each day. If one died, they'd simply move on to the next one.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: They called it... testing their luck.
You feel a knot form in your stomach.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: In WhiteSands, power belongs to whoever controls the supplies. With food and water at their disposal, they could make the rules about who lived and who died.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: The children who died were simply dismissed as having bad luck. After a night's sleep, the children would wake to face another day worrying whether they'd be lucky enough to survive.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: And something as intangible as luck only bred deeper fear.
She fiddles with the coin between her fingertips. Under the harsh ceiling light of the interrogation room, it appears lusterless.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: We lived each day in terror, fearing that fifty percent chance. Every day of survival felt like it had been pried from the tight grasp of luck itself.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: Miguel's leg had been badly beaten the night before. If he had been selected to enter the tomb, it would have been death for him.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: So that day I went into the tomb in Miguel's place. And that's when the cave-in happened.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: Folks in WhiteSands all know that hardly anyone has ever survived a cave-in...

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: But I did, and I brought back the most valuable treasure from that tomb.
You recall her tension in the escape room when she thought you had been swallowed by quicksand, the trembling she tried to hide beneath her calm exterior.
You've personally experienced the dangers of tomb raiding in the escape room. An actual WhiteSands tomb would only present a far more extreme survival challenge beyond imagination.

options: That's why back in the escape room...

choices.text: That's why back in the escape room...

steps.content: Remembering how she nearly lost her composure in the escape room, Lysandra awkwardly shifts the thin stick in her mouth, her eyes darting away as she speaks in a subdued voice.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: Your big city sure has the craziest technology. Even fake things are made to seem so real.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: After all, experiences like this will never feel just like a game for me.
She leans back in the interrogation room chair and flips her coin into the air.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: The game of the coin was a game of life and death. So, why would you call it a lucky charm?

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: This coin that almost got me killed in the tombs countless times?
She snatches the falling coin in one swift motion, the corners of her mouth curling into a widening smile that contains not a trace of joy.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: I survived with my knowledge of WhiteSands, with what I remembered from what those geezers said about the tombs every day, with the skills to escape quicksand and locate solid sandstone structures during scouting. It was all me.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: But those geezers...

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: They said it was only because I was lucky.
The smile fades from her face. You watch her, feeling a complex mix of emotions yourself.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: How ridiculous.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: The moment I climbed out, I knew that my life was in my hands alone.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: By relying on myself alone, I could become someone who changed the rules—who made the rules. I could truly gain the power to fight back.
She casually tosses the coin onto the desk and looks directly into your eyes, her piercing gaze seeming to cut right through you.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: As I became more skilled, I obtained more resources from them, which meant the children received more from me.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: Because of me, they survived safely and no longer lived in constant fear. I gradually took control of the situation.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: Eventually, I got better and better, quietly memorizing everything they ever showed me. Scouting tombs, identifying treasures, gathering intel, finding contacts, negotiating deals.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: Funnily enough...
Her lips twist into a bitter smile.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: I actually began to enjoy the process.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And then, you became infected with Mania...
She smiles sardonically again.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: After the trade restrictions got stricter, on a completely ordinary day, they discovered another tomb, one that was ancient and lethal.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: As usual, I volunteered to go. No one objected.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: So, that tomb expedition was what got them killed?
She answers without hesitation.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: Yes. That was also when I got infected with Mania. When I emerged carrying the most valuable treasures they'd ever seen, those geezers couldn't believe their eyes.
(Flashback)
Clank, clank, clank. The sound of precious antiquities tumbling out of a tattered sack.
One hand after another reaches into the pile of treasures.

steps.speaker: Old Fernando
steps.content: ...Lysandra, I swear, your luck is something else! How do you always manage to dig up the most valuable treasures?

steps.speaker: Old Fernando
steps.content: If the other kids had even half your luck, we'd all be more than satisfied!
A blood-stained hand tosses the number eight coin back into the bag of old coins.
Seeing Lysandra covered in wounds, her body marked with strange patterns, electric sparks constantly crackling from her hands, the old men's eyes grew wider and wider with shock.

steps.speaker: Then I'll make you spit out everything you've devoured.
steps.content: Wait, wait a second... You went into that tomb and came out a Sinner?! The beasts down there can't kill you anymore, can they?!

steps.speaker: Old Fernando
steps.content: Wow, it's just unbelievable... Talk about hitting the jackpot!
As if struck by an idea, Old Fernando's expression morphs from terror to greed. He begins kicking the children on the ground, shoving them toward the entrance of the ancient tomb.

steps.speaker: Old Fernando
steps.content: You lot, and you over there, get up now, you worthless wretches!

steps.speaker: Old Fernando
steps.content: Move it! All of you, get down in that tomb now!
Lysandra stands panting, the Mania still swirling visibly around her body. A wrench in her scarred hand, she positions herself between them and the terrified, trembling kids.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: What... what are you doing?!

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: I've already been down there! There's Mania in there! Why would you send them down there too?!
Old Fernando, the leader, greedily licks his lips, revealing a gleaming gold tooth.

steps.speaker: Old Fernando
steps.content: Once they're all infected with Mania like you, we'll have more profit-making tools at our disposal!

steps.speaker: Old Fernando
steps.content: Look at how much stronger and more powerful you got! Imagine how many treasures you can dig out now!
He smacks his lips as his face contorts into a menacing grimace.

steps.speaker: Old Fernando
steps.content: You've always volunteered to go down into tombs just to protect them. You're valuable with your treasure-hunting skills. I'll give you that. That's why we've turned a blind eye to your little hero act until now.

steps.speaker: Old Fernando
steps.content: But today, you don't get a say anymore! Supplies are already scarce, so it'll only solve our problem if some of them end up dying. And if they're lucky like you and survive Mania, they'll be even more useful to us...
He advances menacingly, forcing Lysandra and the children to back up until they're nearly at the edge of the tomb pit.

steps.speaker: Old Fernando
steps.content: All of you, get down there now! Argh!!
The wrench strikes his skull with resolute, devastating force.
[End of flashback]

In this cruel game of luck, Lysandra finally took matters into her own hands, ending this insane system. She refused to tolerate the dark side of humanity any longer, completely reclaiming control over her own destiny.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: Just like that, I disposed of them, pushed them into the tomb, and erased any trace of my involvement by staging it as a cave-in.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: I only took this coin with me... as a reminder to never trust fate in those moments when I'll face the unknown and must make a decision.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: To just trust myself.
She says emphatically, concluding her story.
The interrogation is nearly over as you sort through the documents in your hand, alongside everything she's just told you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You've told me everything about your past and what happened to those old raiders. While I can't condone your methods, I wasn't in your position, so I can't easily judge what was right or wrong.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But if I had been under those same circumstances, I think I would have shared your idea.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Breaking free from the game of life or death dictated by luck, and instead making your own rules. That is what it means to trust in yourself and take your fate into your own hands.
Your words momentarily catch her off guard. Then, the corner of her mouth turns up slightly, as if a heavy burden has just been lifted from her shoulders.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: ...Thank you.
Yet throughout her entire account, she seems to have deliberately avoided one seemingly insignificant detail.
As she's about to leave the interrogation room, you call out, stopping her in her tracks.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I still have one last question.

options: What happened to those children in the end?

choices.text: What happened to those children in the end?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Throughout your entire story, you've left out one seemingly insignificant detail...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: What happened to those kids in the end?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: After you got rid of those old raiders, whenever the children's whereabouts came up, you either claimed you didn't know or deliberately changed the subject.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'm curious. If you went as far as abolishing the rules of luck to protect them, surely you'd care about what happened to them afterward.
A heavy silence falls. The briefly lightened atmosphere now feels even more suffocating.
You wait quietly. You know Lysandra will give you an answer.

Perhaps it's the determined way she guided you through that escape room, the brief panic in her eyes when you fell from the balance scale, or how she refused to let you go when you were sinking into the quicksand.
It's the trust she's built with you during that escape room challenge. You just know that even though she might try to avoid the topic or ignore her own feelings, she will ultimately answer you.
She finally speaks, her face hidden in shadow, her voice painfully hoarse.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: I don't know.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Why?
Another strained, uncomfortable silence.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: ...After I took out those bastards, I let the children go.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: I gave them all the money I had and everything else I'd gathered. Told them to get as far away as possible and never come back.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Then?
You study her intently, but she keeps her lips tightly pressed together, refusing to meet your eyes.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Lysandra, what do you fear?
Something suddenly clicks for her. She lurches forward, staring directly into your eyes.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: Why do you keep asking about where they went... Did you find them? Are they still alive?

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: They're not dead, are they?
Before you can even answer, Lysandra takes a deep breath, her hand trembling as she tightens her grip on the coin, and interrupts you.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: No, don't answer me.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: ...They could barely buy any food or water in WhiteSands with the scraps I gave them. Miguel and Yulen had always been sickly... they couldn't have survived long.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: They couldn't have survived at all...
Lysandra falls silent.

She finally recalls that moment she thought had already been lost in her memory. The farewell beneath the blood-red moon. All those pairs of mournful eyes. That instant which still cuts through her heart every time she flips her coin.

She took back control over the children's lives from those old raiders, only to repeat their cruelty after her impulsive action left her unable to establish a new shelter for them. That game of luck she once sneered at played a cruel joke on Lysandra in the end.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: Hah... In that final moment, I told them to... try their luck. To see how long they could survive on their own.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: I was just like those old bastards. I did the same thing... I left those barely clothed children alone to fend for themselves.
Lysandra stares helplessly at the coin, her eyes trembling with anguish.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Listen, Lysandra.
You approach her, leaning down to meet her troubled gaze directly.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I know you did your best back then.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You already did what you could to protect them... You destroyed that cruel system under those harsh circumstances.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I know, in WhiteSands, you couldn't all survive with the meager resources you had.
You gently guide her gaze away from the coin, directing her attention to you instead.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You're good at calculating the odds of success and failure, right? In that situation, you must have done the same. You weighed the two options: everyone dying together, or you surviving while giving others a chance to find their own path to survival.

It is precisely because she always relies on these meticulous calculations that she has spent countless sleepless nights rethinking which choice would have given them the better chance of survival. Yet the endless calculations have never truly convinced her, because she continues to blame herself for one thing—that she chose to leave it all to luck in that crucial moment.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You did your best, Lysandra.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You did everything you could.
You repeat these words over and over, your voice growing softer each time, trying to soothe Lysandra as she collapses under the weight of guilt and self-blame.

You believe in her, just as you did in that escape room. You know she'll once again work through her pain, confusion, and anxiety, allowing her usual analytical mind to return, once again finding back the Lysandra who refuses to leave it up to fate.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You need to accept that... there are things you can't do.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: We can't control everything, every twist and turn of our stories. Even if we remain perfectly calm and cautious and calculate every possibility, it's still impossible to take responsibility for others' fates when making a decision.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Don't let your pride get to you, Lysandra.

Lysandra slowly draws her unfocused gaze back from the shadows and fixes her eyes on your face, like a machine receiving commands for the first time after a complete shutdown from suppressing its emotions for too long.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You know better than anyone that one should always rely on oneself and control one's own fate...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: So what makes you think the children shouldn't do the same? Isn't that exactly what you wanted to teach them?
You smile at her.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: What...
Her eyelashes flutter as she seems to be analyzing the meaning behind your smile.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I investigated. They all survived, every single one of them.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: They... all survived?
The light slowly returns to her lifeless eyes as you watch her quietly, offering your silent support.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: They all survived, every single one of them.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Took the MBCC some effort to look into that. But fortunately, the results were good. Miguel became an apprentice in a merchant caravan. Yulen works as a guard at a DisCity border station, and then there's Logan...
You lay out evidence of their updates one by one as Lysandra examines each photo with disbelief, carefully identifying their appearances.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You saved them, Lysandra. Just as you saved me in that escape room.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: What truly protected me and allowed me to wake up in the end wasn't luck.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But that you remembered to secure my rope in the last moment so that I could dodge the overturning balance scale, and your voice calling out to me...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: That got me back on my feet.
She slowly sits down.

Your words wind their way into the depths of her heart, gently loosening the knot of guilt and self-blame she's carried for so long. At last, the light returns to Lysandra's eyes as she looks at the photos before her and smiles faintly.

She imprisoned herself in that night when, left with no other choices, she had to betray her own belief and rely on luck. And ever since then, she's forbidden herself from forgetting, forcing herself to remember by flipping the coin over and over again.
Lysandra shifts slightly, the corner of her mouth lifting in a relieved smile.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: ...Even though I couldn't catch you when you fell?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It was only an escape room.
You shrug, like she does all the time. When she genuinely smiles, a tiny dimple appears at the corner of her mouth. It vanishes so quickly that you wonder if you imagined it.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: I'll accept that there are things I can't do, but that won't stop me from giving my best shot...

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: Is that enough?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Yes, that's enough.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Don't be so hard on yourself.
You pick up the coin and place it back in her palm. Her skin is warm, the metal connecting your shared warmth.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You don't need the coin to remind yourself what you must accomplish. You've already accomplished all your decisions with your efforts.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You are stronger than fate, destiny, or luck could ever be.
[Exiting Interrogation Room - Scene Transition]
A few days later...
After processing the final approval for shutting down that new escape room in Eastside, you close your eyes, feeling somewhat exhausted.

You recall the multiple reports you've submitted to your superiors requesting leniency for Sinner Lysandra's crimes, along with the numerous attempts of vouching for her personally. With the outcome still uncertain, you can't help but worry.
Someone knocks on your window frame, interrupting your thoughts. You turn to look.
The person yanks your window open, then leans against the frame with crossed arms, fiddling with a thin stick with her lips.
Before you can identify who it is, Roulecca bumps that figure aside and pops up energetically.

steps.speaker: Roulecca
steps.content: Hey, hey! Caught by Roulecca again! Lysandra, you've been hanging around Chief's office an awful lot lately...

steps.speaker: Roulecca
steps.content: Are you planning to sneak out again? Hey, you're not allowed to go out and have fun without Roulecca!
[Lysandra's portrait]

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: Of course not.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: I came to invite Chief to another escape room. I heard a new one just opened.

steps.speaker: Roulecca
steps.content: Huh? Another escape room? Count me out then. I thought about it. With Roulecca's talent, solving those dead people's puzzles is only gonna get more boring.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: Perfect. You can just stay at the MBCC and nurse your injury, kid.

steps.speaker: Roulecca
steps.content: Heyyy! Chief, I've changed my mind! Roulecca wants to go with you after all, and crush those puzzles with my luck before Lysandra gets to show off!

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: I don't mind. As long as he's okay with it.
steps.female_content: I don't mind. As long as she's okay with it.

steps.content: As Roulecca keeps protesting, you notice Lysandra staring at you quietly.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Yes?

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: Why not settle this with a little game?
She looks at you like she's discovering an uncharted ruin that's mysterious, dangerous, and irresistibly tempting to Lysandra the tomb raider.
Ting-a-ling...
A familiar coin is flipped high into the air before your eyes and falls back down.
But this time, instead of clutching it in her palm as usual, she presses the coin on the back of her other hand, covering it.
The two of you exchange a smile.

steps.speaker: Lysandra
steps.content: Take a guess, Chief. Heads or tails?
